title: Heterogeneous probe scheduler for profile stability and runner affinity
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Add a scheduler and coordinator to the benchmark harness that runs heterogeneous probe mixes (datasets, prompt perturbations, and eval runners) with deterministic sampling and runner affinity tagging so published performance profiles are stable across model onboardings and version pins. This ticket scopes design, implementation, and a minimal publish pipeline to validate profile repeatability and surface variance to the Console.
acceptance_criteria: Scheduler can express multi-dataset probe mixes with weights and deterministic seeds
Eval runners accept an affinity tag and the harness pins runs to runner groups consistently
Published profile artifacts include run-level metadata (seed, dataset-slice, runner-affinity, prompt-variant) as a flat TSV or JSONL referenceable from the Console
Profile repeatability: across three independent full-profile runs against the same model version, 95th-percentile latency and token throughput variance <= 5% and median quality metric variance <= 2%
Automated validation job runs post-publish that compares new profile against pinned baseline and flags regressions above thresholds
Docs updated: runner-shim README, profile-schema.md, and a short migration note for onboarding engineers
tasks: Design probe scheduler DSL and manifest format (dataset slices, weights, seed)
Implement scheduler core in harness and a deterministic sampling module
Add runner-affinity tagging and enhanced runner selection algorithm
Instrument eval runners to emit required flat metadata fields per probe
Extend profile publisher to include run provenance and version pin references
Create a Console import hook to surface profile variance and regression alerts
Write integration tests covering deterministic sampling and affinity pinning
Author docs and runbook for model-onboarding teams
